description: The bar chart titled “SimpleQA performance over the course of post-training” illustrates how model behavior evolves across four stages—Base, SFT, DPO Stage 1, and Final—by categorizing responses to SimpleQA problems into three mutually exclusive outcomes: “Correct” (green), “Not Attempted” (dark blue), and “Incorrect” (light blue), with percentages summing to 100% per stage. The vertical axis represents percentage (%) on a linear scale from 0 to 100, with tick marks at 20-unit intervals. At the Base stage, the model correctly answers 6.8% of questions, incorrectly answers 90.0%, and leaves 3.2% unattempted. After SFT, correct answers drop slightly to 3.7%, incorrect answers fall to 38.7%, and unattempted responses rise sharply to 57.5%. By DPO Stage 1, correct answers further decline to 2.9%, incorrect answers drop to 17.4%, and unattempted responses increase to 79.8%. In the Final stage, correct answers are 3.0%, incorrect answers are 15.8%, and unattempted responses reach 81.1%. The chart visually emphasizes a clear trend: as post-training progresses, the model increasingly avoids attempting SimpleQA problems—particularly those it would likely answer incorrectly—thereby reducing hallucinations, even though this results in a lower simple-evals F1 score compared to the base model, as noted in the accompanying caption.
